Hi Anita —

Thanks for the RFP and the clear asks. I pulled together a short commercial sketch and an attached workbook (Redwood_Termsheet_NodeSwap_v1.xlsx) showing three packaging scenarios:

1) Node licenses (per-GPU) + per-node platform fee: predictable throughput, lower marginal scale cost
2) Seat-anchored operator licenses (per-concurrent-operator) + higher platform fee amortized over seats: easier budgeting for small scale
3) Hybrid: node pool for inference + seat licenses for management/ops; includes burst credit bucket

Key notes up front:
- We can amortize the platform fee over 36 months or treat it as an annual subscription — finance prefers 36-month amortization for capital treatment.
- Unused committed node hours can be converted to support credits at 40% of the pro-rated platform fee in Year 1, 30% thereafter (we can negotiate higher conversion for multi-year commits).
- Migration retainer estimates: $45k flat for a single-site pilot, $120k for a 3-site phased rollout (includes runbook creation, PKI tie-ins, SRE training).

I put the simple TCO tables on the first sheet: Year1 TCO, Year2 scaled TCO, and a sensitivity toggle (2x, 3x). Also mapped support tiers: Bronze (8x5, next-business-day), Silver (8x5, 4-hr response), Gold (24x7, 1-hr response + on-call), Platinum (24x7, 30-min response + named SRE).

Please review and tell me which anchors you want to prioritize. If useful, I can break the node pricing by GPU class (A100/RTX-class).

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
